claim:
Let \(n>1\) be odd and composite, let \(\zeta\) be a primitive \(n\)-th root of unity, let \(K=\mathbb Q(\zeta)\), and let \(c\in\mathbb Z\) with \(c
e1\). Put \(u_c=\zeta+c\zeta^{-1}\). For each divisor \(m\mid n\), define \[R_n(m)=\prod_{p^e\parallel n,\ p^e\mid m}p^{e-1}(p-2)\prod_{p^e\parallel n,\ p^e
mid m}p^{e-1}(p-1),\qquad E_n(m)= rac{R_n(m)-\mathbf 1_{m=n}}2.\] Then \(\mathbb Q(u_c)=K\) and \[[\mathcal O_K:\mathbb Z[u_c]]=|1-c|^{\varphi(n)/2}\prod_{m\mid n,\ m>1}|\Phi_m(c)|^{E_n(m)}.\] Consequently, among all integers \(c
e1\), \(u_c\) is a power-basis generator of \(\mathcal O_K\) if and only if \(c=0\). The excluded boundary \(c=1\) generates the maximal real subfield rather than \(K\).
integrity: The infinite statement is proved by a discriminant factorization and an exact Chinese-remainder count of unit-pair sums. The bundled finite replay is only a consistency check, not a substitute for the proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to odd composite conductors and integers c other than 1. It does not treat even or prime conductors and does not classify power-basis generators outside the one-parameter family zeta+c zeta^{-1}.
title: Exact composite-conductor index for \(\zeta+c\zeta^{-1}\)
